newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie buys DASfleet from Canberra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie buys DASfleet from Canberra.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said Macquarie Bank Ltd had acquired the Australian government's vehicle fleet management company DASfleet for A$407.9 million.
"Macquarie will buy DASfleet, a business unit of the Department of Administrative Services, for A$407.9 million," Fahey said in a statement.

DASFLEET, which covers more than 16,340 cars, is the sole supplier of passenger and commercial vehicles to the majority of Australian government departments and agencies, Macquarie said in a separate statement.
DASFLEET acquiries between 7,000 and 11,000 new vehicles every year and the fleet includes passenger cars, wagons, motorbikes and commercial vehicles, Macquarie said.

"We regard this as a medium to long term strategic initiative, and therefore it will have no material short term impact on the bank's profitability," Macquarie managing director Allan Moss said in the statement.

Macquarie Bank division director Kerrie Mather, who is responsible for the bank's motor vehicle fleet leasing business, said most of the acquisition consideration relates to the vehicles which are funded under a lease and a small amount relates to acquisition of other assets.
Mather said Macquarie may syndicate some of the funding.
"We have a five year contract with the Commonwealth government to manage the fleet and we have sub-contracted some of the services to Serco," Mather said.
She said after the DASFLEET acquisition Macquarie would have a fleet of over 45,000 vehicles.
